title: Build tinyosc cleanly with strict aliasing enabled
problem: ESP-IDF 6.1 rejects tinyosc's float and double serialization because it reads floating-point objects through integer pointers, violating C strict-aliasing rules.
reproduce: Compile tinyosc.c with GCC, optimization, -Wstrict-aliasing=2 and -Werror=strict-aliasing; the pinned baseline fails at the float and double casts in tosc_vwrite.
acceptance: The unchanged regression fails twice on the baseline and compiles on the candidate; the candidate emits the exact expected OSC bytes for 3.25f and -9.5 and parses both values back correctly.
repair: Copy each floating-point bit representation into a same-sized integer with memcpy before converting it to network byte order.

verification.limitations: BCL reproduces the reported GCC diagnostic and verifies exact OSC float/double serialization on Linux. It does not run the complete ESP-IDF 6.1 firmware build or flash an ESP device.
verification.ownerCheck: Update the component in the ESP-IDF 6.1 project, rebuild with the existing warning-as-error settings, then send one OSC float and double message to the normal receiver and confirm both values arrive unchanged.

negative.outputIncludes: dereferencing type-punned pointer will break strict-aliasing rules

upstream.suiteOutputIncludes: PASS: strict-aliasing compile and OSC float/double wire bytes

publish.commitMessage: fix: avoid strict-aliasing violations in OSC serialization
